decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already captures the entailed one-commission-and-one-ticket rule for each primary mint and the secondary-sale exclusion. Registration of randomly assigned rewards belongs to the accounting Requirement and does not require another change here.

The FAQ already states that no-code mints send commissions and tickets to a random existing NFT holder. The source reports an accounting-registration rule and problem, not a required FAQ wording change.
The source does not change either validation-feedback message; it concerns registration of randomly assigned commissions and tickets after minting.
Requiring primary-mint commissions and tickets to be registered does not alter the configured winner-selection method, eligibility, weighting, or randomness provider.
The accounting rule does not change how NFT mint numbers become referral codes or where those codes are displayed.

The coded-referral reward already awards a $5 commission and one Small Block ticket per successful coded referral. The reported registration problem specifically concerns rewards assigned at random and does not change the coded-referral rule.
The source does not change the $15 mint split or any allocation amount; it clarifies reward accounting and registration after allocation.
The source does not change which referral codes are valid or the self-referral restriction.
The secondary-market exclusion applies to commissions and tickets, not prize-pool funding. Secondary royalties may continue funding the prize pool unchanged.
The accounting rule is independent of the deferred Transak provider, payment methods, wallet provisioning, and fiat mint-delivery flow.
The source concerns commission and ticket accounting rather than whether a successful primary purchase delivers the NFT ebook.
The source does not change the USDC approval-and-mint flow; it concerns downstream registration of randomly assigned rewards.
